newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SPAIN STRIKE THREATENS BELGIAN FORD UNIT.
newsitem.headline: SPAIN STRIKE THREATENS BELGIAN FORD UNIT.

text.p: A 12-day-old strike by Spanish lorry drivers may cause temporary unemployment at Ford Motor Co's Belgian factory which has been scrambling in recent days to obtain spare parts, flying some of them in by helicopter.

"The situation is critical," Ford Genk director Peter Heller told Reuters by telephone on Monday. "But...we have enough spare parts until tomorrow. We have been able to obtain parts...by helicopter and with cars."
But about 10,000 workers would be laid off temporarily if the situation in Spain deteriorated, he said.
Genk, a division of Ford's German unit Ford Werke AG, exports 96.5 percent of its production and accounts for 40 percent of total car exports from Belgium.
The plant produced about 370,000 Mondeo saloon cars and about 68,000 Transit vans in 1996.
Heller said Ford Genk obtained about 800 different spare parts for the Mondeos and Transits from between 150 and 200 different suppliers in Spain.
Only a limited number of the parts had to be airlifted by helicopter, he added.
Striking drivers are demanding a lowering of the retirement age to 60 from 65, recognition of professional illnesses and controlled fuel prices.
The Spanish government earlier ordered security escorts for trucks after the strike jammed up border crossings, cut off roads, blocked ports and disrupted the supply of goods to northern Spain.
